assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the campaign analysis and the final assessment.

faq.q: Do I need a business to practise on?
faq.a: No. The labs use a small cafe as the example, and the practical tasks suggest real local businesses or school clubs.

faq.q: Does it teach a specific ad platform?
faq.a: No. Platforms change every year; the principles of customers, copy, measurement and honesty do not.

faq.q: Is this enough for a marketing job?
faq.a: It is a solid foundation. Employers also look for experience, so try the practical tasks on a real project.

activities.title: Write a customer persona
activities.objective: Describe a typical customer clearly enough that a writer or designer could picture them.
activities.scenario: A new cafe near a college, called Chai and Co., wants to attract students. Write a one-page persona for its main customer.
steps: Give the persona a name and a title as a heading.
Write short lines (a list) covering age and situation, what they want, what frustrates them and where they spend time online.
Add a sentence on what would make them choose this cafe.

checks.label: A heading with the persona's name
checks.hint: Make the first line a heading, such as Persona: Riya, 19.
checks.explain: A named persona is easier to picture and to talk about.

checks.label: At least four short lines in a list
checks.hint: Use the bullet button for age, goals, frustrations and online habits.
checks.explain: Lists keep a persona quick to scan.

checks.label: A goal is described
checks.hint: Include the word Goal or Wants.
checks.explain: Marketing starts from what the customer wants.

spec.what: a line about what the customer wants

checks.label: A frustration is described
checks.hint: Include the word Frustration or Problem.
checks.explain: A persona's frustrations are what your product can relieve.

spec.what: a line about what frustrates them

checks.label: Online habits are described
checks.hint: Mention where they spend time online, such as Instagram or YouTube.
checks.explain: It tells you which channels to use.

checks.label: Between 50 and 220 words
checks.hint: A persona fits on one page.
checks.explain: Short personas get read and used.

activities.title: Write a short advert
activities.objective: Write copy with a headline, two benefits and a clear call to action.
activities.scenario: Chai and Co. wants a social post that offers a student discount. Write it so it is short, clear and persuasive.
steps: Write a headline as a heading that promises a benefit.
Add a bulleted list of two or three benefits (not features).
Mention the student offer.
End with a call to action that says exactly what to do.
Keep the whole advert under 80 words.

checks.label: A headline
checks.hint: Make the first line a heading.
checks.explain: The headline decides whether anyone reads on.

checks.label: Two or more benefits in a list
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Benefits tell people what is in it for them.

checks.label: The student offer is mentioned
checks.hint: Include the word student.
checks.explain: Your offer is the reason to act now.

checks.label: A clear call to action
checks.hint: Use a verb such as Visit, Join, Order or Try.
checks.explain: People act when told what to do next.

spec.what: a call to action such as Visit or Order

checks.label: Under 80 words
checks.hint: Cut every word that does not help.
checks.explain: Short copy is read; long copy is skipped.

activities.title: Write a marketing email
activities.objective: Write a short, honest email with a subject line, a body, a call to action and an unsubscribe note.
activities.scenario: Send existing customers of Chai and Co. a message about a new monsoon menu.
steps: Start with Subject: and a short, clear subject line.
Greet the reader (Hello).
Write two short paragraphs: what is new and why it matters.
Include a call to action.
End with a line that says how to unsubscribe.

checks.label: A subject line
checks.hint: Begin with Subject: and a short line.
checks.explain: The subject decides whether the email is opened.

checks.label: A greeting
checks.hint: Write Hello and a first name or a friendly phrase.
checks.explain: A greeting makes the email personal.

checks.label: Two paragraphs of real sentences
checks.hint: Each with at least eight words.
checks.explain: One idea per paragraph.

checks.label: A call to action
checks.hint: Tell the reader what to do next.
checks.explain: An email without a next step wastes the opened rate.

checks.label: An unsubscribe line
checks.hint: Add a line that says you can Unsubscribe at any time.
checks.explain: People must be able to opt out; it is also the law in many places.

checks.label: Parts in a sensible order
checks.hint: Subject, then Hello, then the body, then Unsubscribe.
checks.explain: Readers expect this order.

activities.title: Compare three channels
activities.objective: Calculate click-through rate, cost per click, conversion rate, cost per sale and return on ad spend.
activities.scenario: Last month Chai and Co. spent on three channels. Work out which one worked best.
steps: In G2 work out the click-through rate: clicks divided by impressions.
In H2 the cost per click: spend divided by clicks.
In I2 the conversion rate: conversions divided by clicks.
In J2 the cost per acquisition: spend divided by conversions.
In K2 the return on ad spend: revenue divided by spend.
Do the same for rows 3 and 4, and in B7 name the channel with the highest return using IF and MAX.

checks.label: G2 is the click-through rate for search
checks.explain: CTR shows how many people who saw it clicked.

checks.label: H3 is the cost per click for social
checks.explain: CPC is what each click cost.

checks.label: I4 is the conversion rate for email
checks.explain: The conversion rate is the share of clickers who bought.

checks.label: J2 is the cost per acquisition for search
checks.explain: CPA is what each sale cost.

checks.label: K4 is the return on ad spend for email
checks.explain: ROAS compares revenue with what you spent.

checks.label: B7 names the best channel
checks.hint: =IF(K2>=MAX(K2:K4),A2,IF(K3>=MAX(K2:K4),A3,A4))
checks.explain: Pick the channel whose ROAS equals the maximum.

activities.title: Which version won?
activities.objective: Compare two versions of a page by their conversion rates and lift.
activities.scenario: Chai and Co. tested two versions of the order page. Work out which converted better and by how much.
steps: In D2 and D3 work out each version's conversion rate.
In B5 find the lift of version B over version A: (B rate minus A rate) divided by A rate.
In B6 show the winner with IF.

checks.label: D2 is version A's rate
checks.explain: The conversion rate is orders divided by visitors.

checks.label: D3 is version B's rate
checks.explain: Same calculation for version B.

checks.label: B5 is the lift
checks.explain: Lift says how much better B is, in relative terms.

checks.label: B6 names the winner
checks.explain: The version with the higher rate leads, though a small test may be chance.

activities.title: Split a marketing budget
activities.objective: Turn percentage shares into amounts and check that they add up.
activities.scenario: The monthly budget is 1,00,000 rupees. Turn each channel's share into rupees and check nothing is left over or overspent.
steps: In C3 work out the amount for the first channel: its share times the budget in B1 (lock B1).
Fill C4 to C7.
In B8 total the shares and in C8 total the amounts.
In B9 show OK if the shares total exactly 100% and the amounts match the budget.

checks.label: C3 is search ads' amount
checks.explain: Each amount is the share times the total budget.

checks.label: C7 is events and offers' amount
checks.hint: Same pattern in row 7.
checks.explain: Locking B1 keeps every row pointing at the budget.

checks.label: B8 totals the shares
checks.hint: =SUM(B3:B7)
checks.explain: Shares should add to 100%.

checks.label: C8 totals the amounts
checks.hint: =SUM(C3:C7)
checks.explain: Amounts should add to the budget.

checks.label: B9 says OK
checks.hint: =IF(AND(B8=1,C8=B1),"OK","Check")
checks.explain: Both checks must pass for the plan to be consistent.

activities.title: Write a campaign brief
activities.objective: Put the plan on one page: goal, audience, message, channels, budget and how you will measure it.
activities.scenario: Chai and Co. will run a two-week back-to-college campaign. Write the one-page brief.
steps: Add headings in this order: Goal, Audience, Message, Channels, Budget, Measures.
Write the goal with a number and a deadline (for example 300 student visits in two weeks).
List at least three channels.
Give the budget in rupees and say how you will measure success.

checks.label: Six headings
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each section.
checks.explain: A clear structure makes the brief easy to approve.

checks.label: Sections in the right order
checks.hint: Goal, Audience, Message, Channels, Budget, Measures.
checks.explain: A brief moves from why to how much to how you will know.

checks.label: The goal has a number
checks.hint: Include a target such as 300 visits.
checks.explain: A goal without a number cannot be measured.

checks.label: At least three channels in a list
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: A mix of channels reaches more people.

checks.label: A budget in rupees
checks.hint: Write the budget, for example 40000 rupees.
checks.explain: Without a budget a plan is a wish.

checks.label: Between 90 and 300 words
checks.hint: One page.
checks.explain: Keep it short enough to read in a minute.

activities.title: Final project: analyse a campaign
activities.objective: Total a four-week campaign, work out its key ratios and decide whether it paid off.
activities.scenario: A four-week campaign ran with 10,000 spend each week. Report its results to the owner.
steps: In B6, C6, D6 and E6 total spend, clicks, sales and revenue.
In B8 find the cost per sale (spend divided by sales).
In B9 the return on ad spend (revenue divided by spend).
In B10 the conversion rate (sales divided by clicks).
In B11 the profit before other costs (revenue minus spend).
In B12 show Profitable or Not profitable with IF, and chart the weekly revenue.

checks.label: B6 totals the spend
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:B5)
checks.explain: Add the four weeks.

checks.label: E6 totals the revenue
checks.hint: =SUM(E2:E5)
checks.explain: Add the four weeks.

checks.label: B8 is the cost per sale
checks.explain: Total spend divided by total sales.

checks.label: B9 is the ROAS
checks.explain: Revenue per rupee spent.

checks.label: B10 is the conversion rate
checks.explain: The share of clicks that bought.

checks.label: B11 is the profit before other costs
checks.explain: Revenue minus spend.

checks.label: B12 says Profitable
checks.hint: =IF(B11>0,"Profitable","Not profitable")
checks.explain: A positive result means the advertising paid for itself.

checks.label: A bar chart of weekly revenue
checks.hint: Chart type bar with labels A2:A5 and values E2:E5.
checks.explain: A chart shows the trend at a glance.
